cosine.d: cos θ: the across part of a length-1 arrow at angle θ (the sine is its up part). cos 0° = 1, cos 60° = 0.5, cos 90° = 0.

map unit.d: On the farm's contour map, one bucket of water and one bag of fertiliser are drawn the same length; that length is one map unit. It is a choice of ruler, and “steepest direction” depends on it.

slice.d: The one-input function you get from a two-input function by freezing one input, like cutting a hill with a vertical knife and looking at the cut edge. The slope of a slice is a partial derivative.

marginal product.d: Economics name for a partial derivative of output: the extra output from one more unit of one input, all other inputs held fixed. On the farm, the marginal product of water is ∂Y/∂W bushels per bucket.

ceteris paribus.d: Latin for “all else equal”. Changing one thing while holding everything else fixed: the idea behind a partial derivative.

isoquant.d: Economics name for a contour line of a production function: all the input mixes that give the same output. Sliding along one swaps one input for another without losing output.

tangent plane.d: The flat tilted sheet that touches a surface at one point and has the same slopes there in every direction. It is the two-input version of the tangent line: ΔY ≈ (∂Y/∂W)ΔW + (∂Y/∂F)ΔF.
